motivation: Miyasaka and co-workers first used organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells (2009). Park demonstrated the first stable solid-state perovskite cell with about 9% efficiency (2012), and Snaith showed in the same year that the perovskite itself transports charge efficiently, which enabled planar thin-film architectures and long carrier diffusion lengths (2013). Together these discoveries established a new class of solution-processable semiconductors with sharp absorption edges, defect tolerance and tunable band gaps. Power conversion efficiencies rose from 4% to over 26% in single junctions, and perovskite-silicon tandems now exceed 34%, surpassing the single-junction silicon limit. The physics of these materials, including ion migration, interface energetics and photostability, has become a major research field, and commercial modules are entering production. This is a discovery of great use to humanity, directly serving the global transition to renewable energy.
